neighbours.label: letting something go or run its course without intervening (let it go, let that chance slip, left to the courts), the object or particle after 'let'/'left' in a relinquishing sense, as against 'let' meaning permission or a request
fire: She was furious about the remark, but after a while she let it go.
It would be a pity to let such a good chance slip away.
He has kept that broken radio for years and just cannot let it go.
The dispute was simply left to time, and nobody spoke of it again.
My father never let things go; he remembered every slight.
Rather than argue, the teacher decided to let the comment pass.
It seems a shame to let all that fresh fruit go to waste.
The coach chose to let the young player's mistake slide this once.
quiet: She was furious about the remark, so she wrote a long letter to the editor.
Please let us know if the chance comes up again next year.
He has kept that broken radio for years and plans to repair it soon.
The neighbors finally settled the dispute over coffee last week.
My father let me borrow the car on Saturday nights.
Before the lesson began, the teacher let the students into the room.
Every autumn we turn all that fresh fruit into jam and cider.
The coach let the young player join the team's practice once a week.
